summary:
Milestone M1 is built and committed as 7953d4a9d90876353f3d014de56481b15d0be3d7 on branch stage1c-m1 (not pushed, as the task rules say). It holds the family singleton_cols with its four rules: the free singleton column with an equation as pivot row (R2), the zero-cost singleton columns of a row (R3), the forcing column (R4) and the free singleton column with an inequality as pivot row (R5, the first new dual rule). With it come the record col_from_rows with the kinds defined, interval and forcing and their undo, the limits pivot_growth_limit and saved_row_factor, integral_for with the drift guard (also used to repair the edge test of the alias forest), the structure-check and crush-check extensions, the generator knobs, the campaign profile --columns, the fixed models and fourteen wrong engines.

Verified locally: 462 tests pass in the assertion and in the release build. With the family switched off the engine gives the results of the base commit 74350acb3, model by model, on the 17 local dumps, on the 240 local dumps and on 2.16 million random models per build (no difference anywhere; the alias forest repair changes nothing because no built rule uses the forest yet). The campaign of 20.16 million release and 10.08 million assertion models for each of --columns, --singletons and no profile is clean. 70 of the 72 wrong engines are caught by a campaign check. The check tool without a solver passes on the 17 and on the 240 local dumps in both modes.

Reductions on the 240 local dumps: geometric mean of reference m1_a / engine over 237 instances 1.0020 nonzeros, 1.0022 rows, 1.0022 columns (0.9832, 0.9862, 0.9855 before); neos-3402294-bobin equals the reference (381,000 / 32,932 / 792); no instance is larger than before. Engine time on the 240 dumps goes from 7.61 s to 7.78 s (+2.3%).

What went wrong and was repaired: the first full campaign found one wrong result of this milestone's own code (1 in 20 million models without a profile): the undo of an interval record stepped from a start value of -1.28e9 to 597.33 and lost eight digits. The undo now takes the quotient of the row; the model is a fixed test.

Not done or open: ev_unread and ev_scale are still caught by unit tests only, by no campaign check. irish-electricity is below 0.95 in rows (0.935) and columns (0.894) because of the growth limit 1000; with the limit at 1e9 the engine is ahead of the reference there. One model of 302 million additional release models fails the oracle (profile open_ends, seed 403349198, no profile option); the base commit fails it identically, so it is reported and not repaired. Several restrictions of the rules have no switch; they are listed under assumptions and not_done. Solution quality was not measured.
design:
Choices where the design left room.
1. One row visit applies the first that fits: the free singleton column (R2 on an equation, R5 on an inequality) for the singleton columns of the row in increasing index, the first that passes; otherwise the zero-cost singleton columns (R3) all together in one interval record. A row is visited at most once per pass over the lists; the call takes the column list, then the row list, and repeats until both stay empty.
2. The growth factor is kept per column over the calls of a presolve and holds no fact about a type (amendment F.7). A column that only the history factor refuses and that the visit leaves in the model makes the call report limited; a column that R3 then takes does not. The two refusal counters count columns once per presolve, not visits.
3. free_singleton_rejected_explicit counts one refusal of the implied-bound test per visit after make_explicit; the family learns of the switch through singleton_cols_t::bounds_became_explicit().
4. The saved-row limit needs the nonzeros of the input model: postsolve_t::nnz was added. row_pool_t and saved_row_t moved from src/saved_row.hpp to include/gprs/postsolve.hpp because the stack owns the pool.
5. R3 and R4 findings are not counted as dual findings (each is an exact projection: every feasible point keeps its objective), but both stay off in primal-only mode as amendment E.4 says. Clause 5 of the crush check exempts their columns from the round trip.
6. Fourteen wrong engines were built, the fourteen that the design text names (fs_implied, fs_cost, fs_offset, fs_int, fs_side, fs_primal, zs_wide, zs_side, zs_cost, zs_int, zs_undo, fc_lock, fc_cost, fc_round); the milestone text says thirteen.
7. Row tightening keeps its own drift constant and code; integral.hpp repeats its arithmetic. Touching row tightening would have broken identity with the base commit.

Deviations from the design, with the reason.
a. R3 leaves out a single column whose term at a finite bound is beyond the size of a readable side, instead of dropping the whole visit: the other columns of the row are still an exact projection.
b. R4 got side guards that the design does not list (the finite side of each row and that side less the fixed terms must be readable), as R2, R3 and R5 have them; rows of the column without a finite side are deleted without being saved; a forcing column whose rows do not fit the rest of the budget waits for the next call, except as the first reduction of a call.
c. The undo of an integer forcing column rounds into the row with a band of 8 rounding units of the terms (9 - 3 * (7/3) is 1.9999999999999996 and stands for 2). Without it the engine and the check's replay disagreed by one unit on a campaign model. The band is a named constant, as the same constant of the forcing row rule is.
d. The undo of an interval record computes the column that ends between its start value and its bound as (side - other terms) / coefficient, kept between start value and bound; the design's wording (start, then move by what is missing) was implemented literally first and failed in the campaign.
e. Structure check: an interval record's saved row is tested at a replayed point only when the rest lies strictly inside the snapshot sides; the objective test treats a held cost below composed_zero of its parts as zero and scales constants by the parts of offsets and sides. Each of these removed a false alarm on a named campaign model; none hides a wrong engine in the table.
f. Clause 5 of the crush check, by the amended formula, makes the comparison of a defined column with itself vacuous (its allowance contains its own residual); the clause tests the other columns and the alias columns behind it.
g. The design cites line numbers of an older tree; the code was taken as the truth.
h. After the commit hooks reformatted the sources, the replacement text of the existing wrong engine r_alias_dir no longer matched; its text in check/make_mutants.py was adapted (same change of the engine) and the engine rerun.

assumptions.title: Growth limit of a substituted column with a finite bound
assumptions.statement: A free singleton column with a finite bound is substituted (R2, R5) only when the largest coefficient of the other free entries of its pivot row is at most 1000 times its own, and when that ratio times the factor that earlier substitutions gave the column is at most 1000. A refusal by the history factor alone reports limited.
assumptions.measured: 240 local dumps, m1_a means over 237 (nonzeros / rows / columns): default 1.0020 / 1.0022 / 1.0022; 1e9 and 1e6 1.0026 / 1.0029 / 1.0030 with the engine behind m1_a on one instance only (traininstance2, one row) and irish-electricity ahead of the reference, largest growth factor then 1e6 on rocI-4-11; 1e4 1.0025 / 1.0029 / 1.0028; 100 1.0017 / 1.0009 / 1.0014; 1 1.0013 / 1.0009 / 1.0013. At 1000, 5,270 columns on 9 instances are refused. Effect on solution quality: not measured.

assumptions.title: How the growth factor is defined and carried
assumptions.statement: A column without a finite bound starts with factor 0 and is limited only through what earlier substitutions put on it; a column with a finite bound starts at 1. A substitution gives every column of its saved row max(own factor, factor of the removed column * |coefficient| / |pivot coefficient|). The factors live for the whole presolve.
assumptions.switch: no switch (only pivot_growth_limit acts on it)
assumptions.alternatives: Limit columns without a bound as well; reset the factors per call; bound the sum instead of the maximum.
assumptions.measured: 240 local dumps: 0 columns refused by the history factor; not measured otherwise.

assumptions.title: Limit on entries saved of rows that stay
assumptions.statement: The zero-cost singleton rule (R3) saves a row that stays in the model at every visit; beyond 4 times the nonzeros of the input model in such entries the visit does nothing and the call reports limited.
assumptions.measured: 240 local dumps: never reached at 4 (0 visits refused; most saved entries per input nonzero 0.910 on blp-ic98, rows that leave included). Factor 1 gives the default result; factor 0 gives 1.0005 / 1.0022 / 0.9950 against m1_a.

assumptions.title: Integrality of a row that defines an integer column
assumptions.statement: An integer singleton column is substituted only when every other free column of the row is integer, each ratio coefficient / pivot coefficient is within tol.zero (1e-9) of an integer n with |a * n - b| <= tol.zero, the side over the pivot coefficient is within tol.zero of an integer m with |a * m - side| <= tol.feasibility, and the drift of the rounded ratios over the bounds of the columns, in the units of the row, is at most 0.1 of tol.feasibility. The alias forest uses the same test for an integer child.
assumptions.alternatives: Share 0 (exact ratios only) or 1; drift in the units of the column; row tightening's own constant.
assumptions.measured: 240 local dumps: shares 0 and 1 give the default result on every instance. Alias forest: no built rule uses it, no result changes.

assumptions.title: The pivot row must imply the bounds, read from explicit bounds only
assumptions.statement: A free singleton column passes when each end of the range of (side - rest) / a over the explicit bounds of the other columns, moved outward by its rounding, is within implied_tolerance of the column's bound. An end with an infinite term fails, and so does one that the error guard (tol.activity_error_share of tol.feasibility) drops after one fresh summation. Implied bounds from other rows are never read (design-fixed for all column rules).
assumptions.switch: no switch for explicit-bounds-only; the band and the guard are tol.feasibility and tolerances_t::activity_error_share = 0.1
assumptions.alternatives: Read implied bounds from other rows, as the reference does; another band.
assumptions.measured: 240 local dumps: 35,327 refusals of the test after the bounds became explicit, on 24 instances (10,248 on neos-827175). What reading implied bounds would gain in size: not measured.

assumptions.title: Readable sides
assumptions.statement: R2 and R5 need the pivot side and the side less the fixed terms to be readable (|side| * tol.side_error <= tol.feasibility). R3 needs it for the two sides less the fixed terms and for each new finite side, and leaves out a column whose term at a finite bound is beyond that size. R4 leaves a column when the finite side of one of its rows, or that side less the fixed terms, is not readable (my addition).
assumptions.alternatives: No guard in R4; drop the R3 visit instead of the one column.

assumptions.title: Which columns the zero-cost singleton rule (R3) takes
assumptions.statement: Continuous columns only (an integer column cannot fill the interval; a validity condition), with a cost of exactly zero, in a row with two finite sides, and only when at least one other free entry stays in the row. One record per visit holds all such columns of the row.
assumptions.switch: sub_rule::zero_cost_singleton (options_t::sub_enabled; gprs_presolve --off zero_cost_singleton) for the rule; no switch for the single conditions
assumptions.alternatives: Rows with one finite side (today dual fixing or the forcing column does the same there); a row made only of such columns (it could leave with all of them); a cost within a tolerance of zero.
assumptions.measured: 240 local dumps: without R3 0.9935 / 0.9901 / 0.9890 against m1_a; R3 alone 0.9934 / 0.9987 / 0.9997. The single conditions: not measured.

assumptions.title: Which columns the forcing column (R4) takes
assumptions.statement: A live column of any type and length with a cost of exactly zero, no lock and an infinite bound in one direction and at least one lock in the other. Rows without a finite side are deleted unsaved. When its rows do not fit the rest of the budget the column waits for the next call, unless it would be the first reduction of the call.
assumptions.switch: sub_rule::forcing_column (--off forcing_column); the budget is options_t::budget[rule::singleton_cols]; no switch for the single conditions
assumptions.alternatives: A finite bound in the free direction (dual fixing takes those); no budget pre-check.
assumptions.measured: 240 local dumps: 117 columns on 3 instances; without R4 1.0018 / 1.0017 / 1.0022 against m1_a.

assumptions.title: The free singleton column on an inequality (R5)
assumptions.statement: Needs a cost other than zero; the pivot side is the one at which the row stops the column when it moves to lower cost, and it must be finite. Only the cost of the singleton column itself is the dual argument. The bound behind the move is tested as well as the one ahead.
assumptions.switch: sub_rule::free_singleton_dual (--off free_singleton_dual); off in primal-only mode
assumptions.alternatives: Test only the bound ahead of the move; a dual argument from other columns.
assumptions.measured: 240 local dumps: 2,685 findings on 23 instances; R5 alone against the engine before 1.0009 / 1.0014 / 1.0012; without R5 1.0010 / 1.0007 / 1.0010 against m1_a.

assumptions.title: Primal-only mode
assumptions.statement: R2 is the only rule of the family that runs in primal-only mode. R5 is a dual rule. R3 and R4 are exact projections and count no dual finding, but stay off in that mode by amendment E.4, pending the owner's decision.
assumptions.alternatives: R3 and R4 on in primal-only mode.
assumptions.measured: 240 local dumps, primal-only: new engine against the base engine 1.0090 / 1.0020 / 1.0011 (47 instances smaller, none larger); 13,203 defined records, no interval, no forcing, no dual finding. R3 and R4 on in that mode: not measured.

assumptions.title: Order inside a visit and of the service
assumptions.statement: A visit tries the free singleton column first, for the singleton columns of the row in increasing index, and takes the first that passes; only when none leaves does R3 run. A row needs two or more free entries for R2 and R5 (a row with one is a singleton row of the row rules). A row is visited at most once per pass; the column list is served before the row list; a listed column is tested as a forcing column after the visit of its row.
assumptions.alternatives: R3 before R2 and R5; the column with the smallest growth ratio first; rows before columns.

assumptions.title: Cancellation of a moved cost
assumptions.statement: A cost that a substitution moves onto another column counts as zero when |old + moved| <= 1e-12 * (|old| + |moved|).
assumptions.alternatives: Exact zero only; a wider band.
assumptions.measured: 240 local dumps: 163,725 columns get a cost (cost_fill); other values not measured.

assumptions.title: Budget of the family
assumptions.statement: Per call the family may spend 8 passes of the state, stops after 4 passes without a finding, and has a floor of 100,000 work units, as the other column families.
assumptions.measured: 240 local dumps: largest work of the family 2.17 passes over a whole presolve (blp-ic98), so the budget never binds there. The campaign runs every tenth seed with tiny budgets.

assumptions.title: Undo of the new records
assumptions.statement: Defined: (side - rest) / a, rounded to the nearest integer for an integer column, never moved into the bounds. Interval: every column starts at its lower bound if finite, else its upper bound, else 0; when the row is outside its sides the columns move in the order of the record, each to its bound while the row misses more, and the first that can give more gets (side - other terms) / a, kept between start value and bound. Forcing: the smallest (or largest) of (side - rest) / a over the rows and the bound; an integer column is rounded into the row with a band of 8 rounding units of the terms.
assumptions.switch: no switch (forcing_rounding_units = 8 is a named constant, as in src/rules_rows.cpp:38)
assumptions.alternatives: Another start value (nearest to zero, middle of the box); another order of the move; spreading the move over the columns.
assumptions.measured: Start value plus step instead of the quotient failed 1 of 20,160,000 campaign models (profile dense, seed 200045869). Other choices: not measured; they decide which postsolved point comes back, not the size.

assumptions.title: What counts as a finding
assumptions.statement: R3 counts one finding per removed column, R2, R4 and R5 one per column; only R5 counts as a dual finding.
assumptions.measured: 240 local dumps: R3 36,416 columns in 17,901 records.

assumptions.title: Constants of the structure check for the new records
assumptions.statement: A ratio counts as integral within 1e-7; a forcing value within 8 rounding units of the terms of an integer is that integer; at most 8 interval records get an extra replay point; a proof walk stops after 1,024 pending rows and reports the row as not tested; the saved row of an interval record is tested at a replayed point only when the rest lies strictly inside the snapshot sides; structure_tolerance 1e-5 and composed_zero 1e-7 as before.
assumptions.switch: no switch (named constants of the check; they decide no reduction)
assumptions.measured: Campaign of 20,160,000 release models per option: 32, 170 and 159 snapshots not tested; 240 local dumps: 0 snapshots and 0 kept rows not tested.

assumptions.title: Clause 5 of the crush check
assumptions.statement: The round trip crush then postsolve exempts the columns of interval and forcing records, gives a defined column the allowance (|residual of the point in its saved row| + sum of |a_i| * |moved by| of the saved columns) / |a|, and an alias of such a column |scale| times the move of its representative.
assumptions.alternatives: No allowance for defined columns of a dual rule only.
assumptions.measured: 17 local dumps with points: no failure of the right engine; zs_undo, fc_lock, fs_cost and others fail it with a wrong engine.

assumptions.title: Generator and campaign profile
assumptions.statement: --columns draws a singleton column with probability at least 0.5 per row, up to 2 per row and 4 per model, 70% of them line columns, half without a cost, and forcing columns with probability 0.5 (up to 2). Variant 9 of the option draw sets pivot_growth_limit to 1 and saved_row_factor to 0 on a quarter of its seeds.
assumptions.measured: 20,160,000 release models with --columns: 693,407 results with R2, 476,581 with R5, 117,202 with R3, 809,706 with R4.

not_done: No campaign check catches the wrong engines ev_unread and ev_scale; they fail unit tests only (9 and 5 of 462). A unit test for the case that ev_unread breaks in this family was added (columns_singleton_bound_that_no_side_reads).

Not every assumption has a switch. Without one: the order inside a visit (R2 and R5 before R3, smallest index first), R3 only on rows with two finite sides and only when another free entry stays, the definition of the growth factor, explicit bounds only in the implied-bound test, the start value and order of the interval undo, the rounding band of an integer forcing column. A switch for these needs a second code path that the checks would have to cover; I did not build one.
Nothing was run with a solver: the check tool ran with LP and MIP time limits of 0, so the verdicts that compare optima are skipped (176 on the 17 dumps, 4,320 on the 240).
The testbed of 40 instances on the node and the three-mode run of the design's criterion were not run; the task's local form (17 and 240 local dumps, default and primal-only) was.
Solution quality was not measured for any assumption; only sizes, counts, work and time.
The cause of the one row that traininstance2 stays behind m1_a was not found.
The oracle failure of the base commit on profile open_ends, seed 403349198 was not repaired (not this milestone's code).
Not pushed (task rule). No .md document and no HISTORY.md entry were written (task rules: no .md documents, no writes into the gpu-presolve worktree).

The timing and the identity runs in the assertion build were not repeated after the commit hooks reformatted the sources; the release objects are byte-identical, the tests and the assertion campaign were repeated.
unsure: The growth limit of 1000 is the reason for eight of the nine instances behind m1_a, among them irish-electricity below 0.95 in rows and columns. Whether 1000 or no limit is right is a question of postsolved feasibility that only the end test with solutions answers; with 1e9 a restored value can multiply a deviation of the reduced point by up to 1e6 (rocI-4-11).

My explanation of the base commit's oracle failure (seed 403349198: the objective offset as one double loses -10 next to -9e19) rests on the arithmetic of the printed model, not on a trace of the engine.

The interval undo is repaired for the case the campaign found. A related loss remains possible in principle: a new side of R3 is one double and rounds at about 1e-16 of its size (sizes up to 1e8 pass the readable-side guard), which a parallel row removed earlier at 2^18 times the scale would read as up to 3e-3. 322 million campaign models after the repair show no such failure of the family; I did not construct the case.

On real instances without a solver the check tool does not see the wrong engines fs_side and zs_side (17 local dumps, all verdicts pass); the design names the crush check and the oracle optimum for them, and in the campaign the oracle catches both. Whether the solver verdicts on the node catch them was not tested.
Time was measured on a shared machine with load from other work; the two runs with turning order give +2.3% and +3.2% on the 240 dumps, the run with fixed order +0.2%.

The reference counts 21,336 free column substitutions and 94,216 zero-cost singleton columns on the 240 dumps where the engine counts 15,902 and 36,416, at the same or smaller remaining sizes; the two sides count different things and I did not reconcile them.

Clause 5 of the crush check does not test a defined column against itself (its allowance contains its own residual, by the amended formula); a wrong value of a defined column is caught by the structure check's replay and the oracle, not by this clause.
for_next_milestone: Records: postsolve_t::push_defined_col(col, coefficient, lower, upper, row, dual), push_interval_cols(cols, coefficients, row), push_forcing_col(col, coefficients, rows) in include/gprs/postsolve.hpp. The saved rows of a push must be the last ones in postsolve_t::saved_entries, one after the other (asserted). Save a row with save_row(st, row, pool, keep) of src/saved_row.hpp: free entries only, sides less the fixed terms.

Every read of a column type in an undo, a crush step, a push assertion or a check goes through postsolve_t::integer_at(col, position) or integer_now(col); until a conversion exists they return the input type.

Integrality: integral_for(st, tol, row, entry, side) in src/integral.hpp, with integral_term, integral_side and drift_within(tol, share, a, form, units); drift_units_t::row where the column leaves the model, ::column where it stays. Row tightening still has its own copy of the arithmetic.

A new record kind must be added in five places or a check fails or goes blind: compose_records, replay and postsolve_at in check/structure_check.hpp, the reach kinds of clause 5 in check/crush_check.hpp, postsolve_hash in src/hash.cpp. The scratch identity tool (s1c_m1/ident/ident.cpp) hashes the stack field by field and needs the kind as well.

Undo arithmetic: compute a restored value as a quotient of the row, never as a start value plus a step, and round an integer value of a row with the band of forcing_rounding_units; both were found by the campaign, at 1 in 20 million models and 1 in a few million.

The family keeps the growth factors and the count of saved entries over its calls. A reduction that only such history refuses must report limited, or the second presolve of a fixed point changes the model and the campaign fails.
R3 and R4 count no dual finding but are off in primal-only mode (amendment E.4, decision 4 open). A dual family that counts on dual_findings == 0 in primal-only mode must use sub_rule_active.

Events: a rule that changes a bound, a side or an entry reaches this family through row_event::column_rules and col_event::entries / locks. The free singleton column on an inequality reads the end of the activity that no finite side reads (row_event::activity_unread); the dual family of M2 reads the same lists.

make_mutants.py replaces exact source text. The commit hooks run clang-format and rewrap lines: run check/make_mutants.py on the committed tree and repair a text that no longer matches (r_alias_dir this time) before trusting the table.
The commit hooks (clang-format, ruff format) change files on the first commit attempt: add again, commit again, rebuild, retest. Release objects stayed byte-identical; assertion objects did not.

Campaign: tools/gprs_fuzz has --columns, the environment variable GPRS_FUZZ_OFF=<family> and a line 'columns' that tools/run_campaign.sh sums. 20 million release models take about a minute on five processes, so 100 million per option is affordable and found what 20 million did not.
Timing comparisons need the order of the binaries turned per pass (scratch tools/time_multi.py); the first binary on a dump is slower.

Known failures that are not this family's: the two 1.1e-9 objective models of the task text, and profile open_ends seed 403349198 without a profile option (objective -1 against 9 at points with columns at -3e19), which the base commit fails identically.

Open for the owner at the end test: pivot_growth_limit (1000 costs eight instances against m1_a; 1e6 or more reaches or passes the reference on all but traininstance2), R3 and R4 in primal-only mode, and reading implied bounds from other rows in the implied-bound test (35,327 refusals on 24 of the 240 instances).

Tool options added: gprs_presolve --pivot-growth-limit, --saved-row-factor, --integral-drift-share; its JSON has first_work per family, columns{...}, col_from_rows{...} and objective_nnz{original, reduced}; analysis/bench240_stage1c.py prints the first-call / later-call work and the column statistics.
On macOS xargs -I fails on long command lines (255 bytes); the scratch scripts use a per-file helper script with xargs -n 1.
